Section heading; CR 400.1-12 carry the zone and object-identity requirements.

The seven normal zones are represented; each seat owns separate library, hand, and graveyard order, while battlefield, exile, command, and stack queries operate as shared game zones across seats. Ante is outside the supported Commander profile.

Hand and library remain hidden-zone categories even when individual cards are known. Graveyard, battlefield, stack, exile, and command are public, with face-down identity visible only to an authorized viewer. Outside the game is no longer misclassified as public.
A card controlled by another seat on the battlefield is inserted into its owner's hand, library, or graveyard and its controller resets to its owner.
Introductory taxonomy sentence; CR 400.4a-b define the prohibited card-type moves.
An instant or sorcery card requested to enter the battlefield remains in its previous zone. The rejection occurs before membership, incarnation, timestamp, visibility, or event mutation.
Conspiracy, phenomenon, plane, scheme, and vanguard objects are outside the supported profile and their command-zone immobility is not represented as a generic type guard.

Library, graveyard, and stack use authoritative ordered lists changed only by typed moves, shuffle, or stack operations. A same-graveyard request is now a no-op instead of silently moving the card to the top.

The bounded destination-replacement capability captures represented ambient sources and every affected object once, resolves contradictory single and simultaneous events in multiplayer APNAP order, and commits only after choice-complete preparation. A closed opponent-card graveyard-to-exile-with-counter wording family lowers to the same typed handler. Aggregate CR 400.6 remains blocked on moving-object self-inspection, destination-viewer inspection, and unrepresented entry and command-zone families.

Ordinary cross-zone moves advance a serialized logical incarnation, clear noncontinued state, and invalidate a target tied to the old incarnation. The separately enumerated CR 400.7a-m continuations retain independent statuses.

The resolving permanent spell keeps its logical incarnation and selected represented entry annotations. Arbitrary characteristic-changing and control-changing spell effects do not use a typed continuation policy.
Battlefield static effects are represented, but a static ability granting a battlefield-functioning ability to a permanent spell is not retained through resolution generically.
Typed damage-prevention primitives exist, but prevention tied to damage from a permanent spell does not continue onto the permanent through a generic identity relationship.
The stack item records selected cost options and payments are authoritative, but complete paid-cost and spent-mana provenance is not transferred to the permanent for later ability queries.
Represented zone-change triggers receive the new public-zone object reference and its logical incarnation while retaining the source's pre-move controller and information.
Selected attachment interactions are compiled, but the complete simultaneous enchanted-permanent/Aura lookup and later unattached-Aura state-action exception are not typed generically.
Selected graveyard cast permissions are validated, but an arbitrary effect-granted cast ability is not retained as an ability of the new stack object.
The physical card reference remains stable internally, but other clauses of an arbitrary cast-permission effect do not receive a typed continuation to the new stack incarnation.
Selected graveyard land-play permissions work, but other clauses of an arbitrary effect do not receive a typed continuation to the new battlefield incarnation.
Represented effects and selected cost snapshots can find a moved public-zone incarnation. The full Oracle effect and cost grammar does not create typed continuation handles for every such move.
Madness and its discarded-card continuation are not represented and remain unavailable under semantic preflight.
Sticker state and public-zone continuation are not represented.
Exile-to-exile advances the logical incarnation and timestamp even though zone membership remains exile; serialization preserves both.
Face-down projection is private, but no supported command turns a face-up command-zone object face down and advances its incarnation.
Command-to-command advances the logical incarnation and timestamp even though zone membership remains command.

An outside-game object has no membership in any player's zone list. Outside is not classified as public; authoritative identity and existing viewer knowledge are retained without inventing zone membership.
Sideboard cards are outside the game by definition. The supported Commander profiles do not include a sideboard, so this record creates no independent runtime behavior claim.
Effects that bring cards into the game from outside and the imported card's end-of-game, owner-leaves, and removal lifecycle are not represented.

Ordinary object resolution excludes outside-game cards regardless of raw reference, and no ordinary legal action exposes them. Printed characteristics remain queryable authoritatively without making the object affectable.
Represented mulligan and shuffle operations iterate card members without mutating a zone object. The generic Oracle grammar for arbitrary instructions that act on every card in a zone is incomplete.
Section heading; CR 401.1-7 carry the structural and behavioral library requirements.

Every noncommander deck card is initialized in its owner's library before opening-hand draws. Remaining library cards retain their initial logical incarnation, while drawn opening cards record the library-to-hand transition; the Commander replacement is separately represented by command-zone initialization.

Each library is one authoritative ordered list whose identities and order are absent from ordinary seat projections. Only represented effects mutate it. A zero-card look now returns no cards rather than exposing the whole library, malformed counts fail before mutation, reorder_top requires the exact known current top group, and shuffle clears tracked positions.
Every seat projection contains lib_n for every active or eliminated player while omitting unauthorized card identities and ordering.

Sylvan Library has an exact owner-ordered top return and reorder_top accepts an explicit top-first group. There is no generic owner-scoped choice when an arbitrary effect puts two or more cards into the same library position simultaneously, particularly for multiple owners, so the general rule remains blocked.

One-shot look and reorder effects are scoped and hidden correctly, but continuous top-card reveal/look permissions are not represented. Consequently the engine cannot freeze the newly exposed top card across every casting, activation, or special-action procedure.

Shuffle correctly removes tracked knowledge, and ordinary zone changes allocate new logical incarnations. The separate CR 401.6 identity transition for a top card that stops and later resumes being continuously revealed is not represented.

The generic library destination accepts any positive N. It inserts with exactly N-1 cards above the card, uses the bottom when the pre-insertion library contains fewer than N cards, rejects invalid positions before mutation, and preserves logical identity when an effect only repositions a card within the same library.
Section heading; CR 402.1-3 carry the structural and behavioral hand requirements.

Game setup draws the configured starting hand size, whose normal default is seven. The generic zone transition can also put cards into their owner's hand without changing the configured maximum hand size.

A player's hand may exceed the normal finite maximum without an early discard. At cleanup the server issues one private exact-count choice, validates distinct cards transactionally, moves the selected cards simultaneously, and replay reproduces the result. Continuous effects that modify or remove the maximum are separately classified under CR 613.11 and are not promoted by this base-zone rule.

Every projection exposes hand_n while ordinary opponents receive no hidden identities or hidden-zone movement names. Owners retain complete hand access outside their priority window and while controlling another player; CR 723.4 adds the controlled hand without replacing the controller's own. A directly observed public-to-hand transition remains in known_hand but does not grant full hand inspection. Hand ordering is private and rules-insignificant.
Section heading; CR 403.1-5 carry the battlefield's structural, scope, permanent-status, identity, and terminology requirements.

The authoritative battlefield is the union of controller-indexed presentation lists, starts empty for every seat, and is queried as one shared target domain. The invariant checker rejects controller/index divergence. Projection keeps a cross-controller attachment in its controller's battlefield list while preserving the attached-object identity.

An omitted target zone canonically means battlefield. Destroy, sacrifice, and bounce operations enforce that ordinary scope, while discard enforces hand scope. Reviewed cross-zone programs must name the zone in their target schema or use an explicit zone-changing instruction; hidden zones cannot be introduced through the public target schema.

The target model derives the permanent category exclusively from current battlefield membership; the same artifact object is a card outside that zone and a permanent on it. Instant and sorcery cards are prevented from entering. Card copies and resolved permanent-spell copies follow their separately reviewed CR 707 object forms while on the battlefield.

Ordinary battlefield entry allocates a new logical incarnation, clears unretained state, and makes a leave-and-return target illegal. The implemented CR 400.7a exception preserves a resolving permanent spell's logical incarnation. Because CR 403.4 imports every CR 400.7 exception and that full matrix is not implemented, the general rule remains blocked rather than being overclaimed.

The engine consumes pinned current Oracle text rather than printed text, and the exact offline Oracle fixture contains no legacy 'in play,' 'from play,' or 'into play' rules wording. The historical aliases therefore require source/data traceability rather than a second runtime zone.
Section heading; CR 404.1-3 carry graveyard ownership, ordinary destinations, public ordered-pile, and simultaneous owner-ordering requirements.

Every player begins with an empty graveyard. Generic destroy, discard, sacrifice, counter, and completed instant-or-sorcery paths append to the owner's graveyard, including when the owner did not control the permanent. Rules-countering a permanent spell now uses graveyard rather than its normal battlefield resolution destination. The exact Dauthi replacement is evaluated before insertion, and a copied spell reaches graveyard before its separately reviewed cease-to-exist state action.

The authoritative list is one ordered pile per owner, with the last element as the top. Projection preserves that order and exposes every face-up identity to every seat. Entry clears face-down status and marks the identity public. Moving a card to the same graveyard is a state-preserving no-op. The engine conservatively provides no ordinary graveyard-reorder action; sanctioned-tournament exceptions remain policy outside this rules engine.

The simultaneous-move primitive snapshots all objects before mutation and assigns a shared timestamp, but same-owner graveyard order is currently inherited from the caller's object sequence. The characterization test proves that no owner decision is issued. Until a resumable, owner-scoped ordering choice is available across state actions and resolving effects, this rule remains blocked and the graveyard mechanic remains untrusted.
Section heading; CR 405.1-6h carry the behavioral and structural stack requirements.

Represented spells, activated abilities, and triggers receive separate stack objects, and abilities do not use an associated card object. Casting still moves the physical card only after choices and payment instead of at CR 601.2a, so proposal-dependent stack characteristics and effects can be wrong.
The ordered stack list stores its bottom at index zero and appends each new object at the top. A spell plus a response resolves last-in-first-out and exact-replays.

Represented simultaneous trigger batches group controllers in APNAP order and collect same-controller order before placement. The rule also covers arbitrary effects putting multiple spells or abilities on the stack simultaneously, which is not a generic engine operation.

Represented stack items freeze the casting, activating, or trigger-time controller and associate a spell with its card object. Complete spell characteristics, ability text-only characteristics, copy/layer interactions, delayed-trigger controller rules, and spell-control effects are not represented generically.

A full active-player/nonactive-player pass round resolves exactly the top object. Starting resolution of a lower object is now rejected without mutation. When the stack is empty, the same full pass round advances the step; both paths exact-replay.
Introductory taxonomy sentence; CR 405.6a-h enumerate the immediate, non-stack categories.

Represented effects mutate authoritative state directly during resolution and are never materialized as stack objects. A represented delayed trigger is stored separately and becomes a triggered-ability stack item only when its later event occurs.

Represented static abilities are queried as continuous characteristics and never become stack objects. This structural pass does not promote the incomplete CR 604 characteristic-defining, attachment, zone-permission, layer, or LKI grammar.

Represented activated mana abilities tap and produce mana immediately, create no stack item, and preserve the priority player. CR 605's generic triggered-mana classification and complete nonmana side effects remain incomplete, so the all-mana-ability statement cannot pass.
The represented land-play special action executes immediately without a stack object. The engine explicitly lacks the rest of CR 116's special actions, so the general rule remains blocked.

Represented untap, draw, combat, cleanup, and boundary actions execute synchronously before or without priority and do not become stack objects. The complete CR 703 catalog and every added-step/phase interaction are not implemented.

Represented state-based actions are evaluated and committed as direct stabilization batches before priority and never become stack objects. This structural pass does not promote the separately blocked, unimplemented CR 704.5 action families.

A concession selected from a represented priority task immediately eliminates that player without a stack object. The public command surface cannot yet concede during resolution, a no-priority turn action, or another seat's decision, so 'at any time' is not satisfied.

Represented elimination immediately removes owned spell cards and controlled ability objects from the stack, preserves hidden identities, and lets a three-player game continue. Complete CR 800.4a ownership, control-effect ending, cease-to-exist, exile, team, and continuous-effect ordering remains incomplete.
Section heading; CR 406.1-8 carry exile movement, visibility, face-down pile, linkage, identity, and terminology requirements.

The shared exile target domain is represented through owner-indexed presentation lists. Objects may remain there, return through an explicit movement instruction, or receive a bounded exact play permission. Every ordinary entry and return remains an auditable zone transition.

The generic zone transition moves card objects into their owner's exile presentation from every represented normal per-card source. Exiling a card spell now atomically removes its StackItem, and the invariant rejects any stack item that references a nonstack card. Whole-graveyard and end-the-turn witnesses exercise batch and stack exile with exact replay elsewhere.

Ordinary exile entry is face up and public, while a manually represented face-down object is redacted from unauthorized pilots and the arbiter. The engine does not generically create face-down exile, distinguish permission to examine from prior knowledge, or persist and revoke that permission across all pile and zone transitions, so the complete rule remains blocked.

Unauthorized target generation uses no hidden front-face characteristics, and ordinary stack entry clears face-down status. Exact face-up Dauthi play permission is covered. The engine cannot yet turn a permitted face-down card face up at precisely the pre-announcement CR 601.2 boundary or support every face-down land and spell path.

The characteristic filter proves an unauthorized viewer cannot use a hidden front to satisfy a creature predicate. No generic permission combines an authorized look with resulting-spell quality validation, so this casting family remains blocked.

The characterization shows two face-down cards as separately referenced public objects with no pile metadata and no ordering or random-selection decision. The required grouping, pile choice, server randomness, and delayed reveal after full payment are therefore explicitly blocked.

Exact effects can attach a source-scoped temporary permission or continue a represented Siege action, but exile storage has no generic pile/provenance partition for arbitrary return instructions or abilities that operate from exile.

Dauthi has an exact void-counter permission, but that witness is not generic recognition of printed linked abilities or an exiled-with identity set. CR 607 remains blocked for the required pairing, copying, and zone-change semantics.

Unlike an ordinary same-zone no-op, exile-to-exile movement removes and reinserts the card, increments its zone-change counter, assigns a later timestamp, and allocates a new logical incarnation. The physical card reference remains stable while all old-object links become stale.
